status: implemented and technically verified; independent subject review and pilot validation not performed
title: Static equilibrium and support reactions
objective: Solve force and torque equilibrium for a rigid body and assess support, contact, and tipping constraints.
alignment: Develops equilibrium within the verified official PHS 231 subject coverage. This teaching sequence, contact model, activities, and assessment choices are proposed platform design, not an official NU syllabus or equipment requirement.

prerequisites.purpose: Force moments, couples, rigid-body geometry, and axis conventions
External force inventory, support direction, and body boundaries
Required static friction versus capacity and unilateral contact
Center of mass and weighted resultants
Integrals of distributed loads; necessary calculations are developed locally

coverage.teaching: Require rest in the selected inertial frame, zero resultant force, and zero resultant moment. Distinguish equilibrium from instantaneously zero velocity and from stability. Use three independent planar scalar equations; name six component conditions in 3D without reducing all 3D problems to a planar sketch.
critical: Force balance alone does not imply rotational equilibrium.
Rest at one instant is not proof that acceleration is zero.

coverage.teaching: Distinguish ideal pins with two reaction components, fixed clamps with a reaction couple, frictionless rollers normal to their surface, tension-only cables along their geometry, and unilateral rough contacts with N>=0 and |f|<=mu_sN. Internal member forces cancel only when the selected system contains both interacting pieces. A two-force member requires exactly two end forces and no separate couple or weight.
critical: A pin supplies no reaction couple in this planar idealization.
A cable cannot realize a negative tension; a supporting surface cannot pull.

coverage.teaching: Use Mz=xFy-yFx with counterclockwise positive, explicitly differing from the preceding rolling lesson's signed clockwise scalar. A couple is origin-independent. Under an origin shift a, Mnew=Mold-a cross resultant force; torque balance becomes origin-independent when force balance also holds. Verify solutions about more than one point without inventing extra independent equations.
critical: Do not count component forces and their resultant twice.
Moving the pivot does not create additional independent equilibrium equations.

coverage.teaching: Integrate a nonnegative line load w(x) in N/m to its force Q=int w dx and moment J=int xw dx. Use centroid J/Q only for Q>0; zero load has no unique centroid. Derive uniform and both triangular limits of a linear load. Distinguish distributed-load centroid, uniform-field center of gravity, and an effective support line shifted by applied couples or a horizontal force at height.
critical: Equal total load with a different centroid gives different reactions.
The height of a horizontal load affects its moment even when its horizontal location does not.

coverage.topic: Beam, cable, ladder, and clamp balances
coverage.teaching: Solve two-support beams with overhangs, a pinned horizontal beam and inclined tension cable, an inclined beam with a horizontal cable, a smooth-wall rough-floor ladder as a paper model, and a fixed-end load inventory. Keep perpendicular lever arms rather than using rod length indiscriminately.
critical: Check every solved support force against its direction and contact law.
Do not turn static demand into a strength rating or a physical setup procedure.

coverage.teaching: Find normal reactions as affine functions of load position and intersect their nonnegative domains with the finite beam. At a zero reaction the model is at a limiting contact state; beyond it the negative candidate is impossible for the stated support. Do not clip a negative reaction and continue claiming equilibrium. The simulation does not predict subsequent tipping motion.
critical: A zero reaction is a boundary, not proof of a robust stable state.
An algebraic solution can violate the support model.

coverage.teaching: For a rough left support and smooth right support, solve required friction from horizontal balance and use the actual left normal force in its bound. A raised horizontal load alters normal reactions. For an ideal rectangular block, compare mu_sW with Wb/(2h) under the stated centered weight and fixed loading height; show sliding-first, tipping-first, and simultaneous thresholds.
critical: Do not use the total beam weight in a friction law attached to only one support.
A friction-limited force and a tipping-limited force are distinct model conditions.

coverage.teaching: Three vertical supports generally leave a reaction family when only rigid-body statics is known. Give an explicit symmetric spring-support compatibility model to select one member of that family, preparing for elasticity. Conversely, three unknowns do not guarantee a unique answer: a pin plus an ineffective horizontal support can leave a rotation mechanism. Use local potential minima, maxima, and constant potential to distinguish stable, unstable, and neutral equilibria, including a quartic minimum with zero second derivative.
critical: Counting unknowns is not a rank or geometric restraint test.
Equilibrium does not establish stability, stiffness, or strength.
Zero second derivative alone does not establish neutral stability.

coverage.teaching: Use independent allowed intervals for moving load, raised horizontal load, and friction coefficient. Derive reaction and friction-margin extrema from monotonicity, state when correlations invalidate independent corner combinations, and report all, none, or mixed admissibility without probability claims. Record system boundary, force inventory, predicted reactions, contact decisions, alternate-origin residuals, and a controlled change.
critical: A small equation residual does not validate the assumed supports.
No physical ladder, suspended-load, elevated-weight, or destructive experiment is assigned.

investigation.model: Rigid horizontal beam on two unilateral supports at a<b. Left support supplies vertical NA and horizontal Coulomb static friction; right support is smooth and supplies only vertical NB. Uniform beam weight W acts at L/2; external linear downward line load w(x) runs across0..L; a downward point load P moves along0..L. Signed horizontal force H is transmitted through an ideal massless rigid attachment at height h, and separate signed CCW couple M acts. Static candidate only; no post-failure dynamics, compliance, strength, damping, or hardware procedure.
investigation.inputs: L1..12m; supports0..L separatedbyatleast.1m; W.1..200N; P0..300N; loadposition0..L; w0,w1 0..100N/m; H-100..100N; h0..4m; M-300..300Nm; mu_s0..1.5. DefaultL6,a1,b4,W60,P60,x3,w0=w1=0,H12,h1,M0,mu_s.4.
investigation.equations: Q=L(w0+w1)/2; J=L²(w0+2w1)/6; D=W+Q+P>0; A=W L/2+J+P x+hH-M. NB=(A-aD)/(b-a),NA=(bD-A)/(b-a),fA=-H. CandidateadmissibleiffNA>=0,NB>=0,|H|<=mu_s NA. DistributedcentroidJ/Q isundefinedwhenQ0. Downwardloadcentroid(W L/2+J+Px)/D differsfromeffectiveverticalreactionlineA/D whenhH-M nonzero.
investigation.outputs: Candidate force inventory, normals, friction demand/capacity/margin, separate failed constraints, vertical-load centroid, effective support line, and force/moment residuals about0,A,B. An affine moving-load sweep includes0,L,selectedposition, and all exact constraint boundaries within0..L; complete equivalent table, reaction-versus-position plot, and clearly labeled location schematic with a complete external force inventory. Show the feasible position interval or explicitly none. Negative candidates remain visible as incompatible requirements, never clipped into a claimed new equilibrium.
investigation.predictions: NA, NB, requiredsignedfriction, and a contact decision: admitted; positive-contact candidate fails friction; or unilateral contact fails. Exact boundary remains admitted but is explicitly marked limiting. Predictions refer to the chosen initial position; the sweep slider then compares positions under otherwise unchanged loading.
investigation.accessibility: Keyboard-controlled numeric inputs, selected sweep slider with Home/End/arrows, exact-boundary buttons, table regions with keyboard overflow, text-identifiable force directions, diagram descriptions, and no automatic motion. Diagram text sized for mobile and tables supply every numerical result.
investigation.limits: No material strength, support compliance, cable elasticity, or dynamic fall is modeled. Static feasibility does not establish global stability or safe hardware loading. The simulation is not a physical ladder, suspended-load, or elevated-weight experiment. Controls reset onreload; notes and assessments persist.

independentChecks: Integrate distributed force and first moment numerically rather than repeating the centroid formula.
Solve the three equilibrium equations by independent small-matrix elimination and verify Cartesian force moments about several shifted origins.
Enumerate reactions over dense position samples and compare membership in the independently intersected unilateral/friction interval, including exact bounds and adjacent points.
Check cable direction components, smooth-wall ladder torque, clamp moment, and support action/reaction recipients.
Verify inferred loads by substituting measured reactions into independent moment balance.
Use compliant-support equations separately to check the statically indeterminate family; test a singular support geometry instead of equating unknown count with rank.
Use nearby potential values and derivative finite differences for local stability, including zero quadratic curvature.
Enumerate uncertainty corners and compare all/none/mixed outcomes without probabilities.
Run at least50 deterministic seeds pervariant with units, equivalentanswers, impossible supportchoices, blank/complex/nonfiniteinputs, and meaningful edgecases.
Complete actual checkpoint, waitforconfirmed save, reload, export/reset/restore question snapshots, answers, evidence, and notes.
edges: Distributed load zero and both triangular limits

resources.title: Conditions for Static Equilibrium
resources.use: Primary textbook coverage check for force/moment equilibrium, torque origins, center of gravity, and tipping. All lesson exposition, examples, diagrams, and generators are original.

resources.use: Optional free primary-source exercise in isolating a body and writing equilibrium equations. Its PDF was opened and checked; no copied problem is used as platform assessment.

assessmentDefaults.meaning: Four questions use the existing proposed 75% checkpoint threshold while requiring both critical support-validity questions. Procedural beam and distributed-load questions remain noncritical. This is a platform teaching choice, not an official NU grading policy.
assessmentDefaults.verification: The 16 variants each pass 50 deterministic independent fixtures. Window variants deliberately include empty, nonempty, and singleton domains; cable signs, unilateral contacts, competing limits, singular restraint, zero-curvature stability, and interval classifications are covered.
